claim: Domestic on-budget sources of recovery funding usually include government operational and capital budgets and special levies or surcharges for recovery.
construction_reason: Paraphrases two of the listed domestic funding sources.

claim: Recovery funding comes entirely from domestic on-budget sources such as government budgets and special recovery levies.
construction_reason: Domestic sources are listed, but 'entirely' is not established; the passage also mentions contracting with funding agencies.

claim: The plan rules out issuing sovereign reconstruction bonds as a source of recovery funds.
construction_reason: Issuing sovereign reconstruction or development bonds is listed as a source.

claim: The Paris Agreement entered into force on 4 November 2016, after at least 55 Parties covering an estimated 55% of global emissions had deposited their instruments.
construction_reason: Restates the entry-into-force condition and date.

claim: The agreement provides for a global stock-take every five years, with the first stock-take required in 2018.
construction_reason: The five-yearly stock-take is stated; a first stock-take in 2018 is not.

claim: India has not ratified the Paris Agreement and has not submitted an NDC.
construction_reason: The passage says India ratified the agreement and submitted its NDC.

claim: Under Section 39 (b), State Government departments may integrate disaster prevention and mitigation measures into their development plans and projects.
construction_reason: Paraphrases Section 39 (b) as quoted.

claim: Section 38 (2) (f) requires every State Government to integrate vulnerability-reduction measures into the State development plan.
construction_reason: The passage says the State Government 'may integrate'; 'requires' turns permission into a mandate.

claim: Section 38 (2) (e) prohibits State departments from including mitigation measures in their development plans.
construction_reason: Section 38 (2) (e) provides for ensuring such integration.

claim: Flood shelters are to be used for purposes such as running schools or anganwadis so that they are properly maintained and in good condition during floods.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the shelter-use and maintenance provision.

claim: State governments will ensure flood shelters are used for schools and anganwadis, with the National Disaster Response Force responsible for their upkeep.
construction_reason: Use through state, district and local authorities is supported; an NDRF upkeep role is added.

claim: Flood shelters should be kept unused between floods so that they remain in good condition.
construction_reason: The passage promotes using shelters for schools and other facilities to keep them maintained.

claim: The national policy treats capacity development as a continuous process that must cope with staff turnover, new recruits and technical change.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the continuous-process challenges.

claim: Capacity development must address staff turnover and new recruits, and every agency must complete a capacity review within its first year.
construction_reason: The challenges are stated; a first-year review deadline is invented.

claim: The NPDM 2009 gives the National Institute of Disaster Management only a minor role in capacity development.
construction_reason: The policy envisages a pivotal role for NIDM.

claim: CGI roofing sheets are non-combustible, and their corrugations help drain water away from the shelter.
construction_reason: Restates two listed properties of CGI sheets.

claim: CGI sheet roofs are lightweight and non-combustible and weigh less than 5 kg per square metre.
construction_reason: Light weight and non-combustibility are stated; the weight figure is invented.

claim: CGI sheets have low thermal conductivity, so they keep shelters well insulated against outdoor temperatures.
construction_reason: The passage lists high thermal conductivity as a limitation.

claim: People are to be made aware of keeping a kit with medicines, a torch, identity and ration cards and non-perishable food ready before the monsoon starts.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the special-kit awareness measure.

claim: Specially designed public awareness programmes are to be developed for women, the elderly and migrant workers.
construction_reason: Women and the elderly are named; migrant workers are not.

claim: Communities should not attempt to make flood rescue devices from household articles.
construction_reason: The community is to be trained to make and use improvised rescue devices from household articles.

claim: Where a temporary shelter needs a foundation, it should preferably be at least 300 mm deep, with variations depending on soil and site conditions.
construction_reason: Restates the foundation-depth guidance.

claim: The plinth of every temporary shelter must be at least 150 mm above the highest expected flood level, with no exceptions.
construction_reason: The passage says 'should preferably'; a strict mandate with no exceptions is not stated.

claim: On soils with low bearing capacity, heavy structures should be built to stay stable.
construction_reason: Light weight structures are recommended where bearing capacity is low.

claim: Flood plain zoning cannot remedy existing situations, but it helps minimise flood damage in new developments.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the stated limit and benefit of zoning.

claim: Flood plain zoning bans all development activity throughout both protected and unprotected flood plain areas.
construction_reason: Zoning limits development in both areas; protected areas still allow low-damage activities.

claim: In protected areas, flood plain zoning allows any development regardless of the damage it would suffer if protection failed.
construction_reason: Only activities that would not involve heavy damage if protection fails are allowed.

claim: The DM Act has no provision for declaring a disaster a 'national calamity', and state governments usually lead disaster management with central support.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the national-calamity point and the supporting central role.

claim: Central agencies generally take part on the state government's request, provided the disaster affects more than one district.
construction_reason: Participation on request is stated; the multi-district condition is invented.

claim: Under the DM Act, the central government formally notifies major events as national disasters and takes over their management.
construction_reason: The Act has no provision for notifying a national disaster; states usually lead.

claim: States were recommended to legislate against unauthorised riverbed cultivation and encroachment into drains, and to strengthen enforcement where such laws exist.
construction_reason: Paraphrases Recommendation 14.

claim: States should legislate against unauthorised riverbed cultivation, with the Central Water Commission enforcing these laws.
construction_reason: State legislation is supported; a CWC enforcement role is added.

claim: The recommendation bans all cultivation in riverbeds, including crops such as watermelons.
construction_reason: Crops like watermelons may be allowed with caution.

claim: One objective of the guidelines is to build flood-resistant features into new structures in flood-prone areas.
construction_reason: Restates objective 4.

claim: The guidelines aim to make all existing and new buildings in flood-prone areas flood resistant.
construction_reason: New structures are covered; all existing buildings are not.

claim: The guidelines shift the focus away from preparedness toward post-flood relief.
construction_reason: Objective 1 shifts the focus to preparedness.

claim: Permanent housing reconstruction often takes two to three years, so affected families need durable intermediate shelters in the meantime.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the rationale for intermediate shelters.

claim: Relief camps in existing public buildings are set up immediately and must be vacated within two weeks.
construction_reason: Relief camps in public buildings are described; a two-week vacating deadline is not.

claim: Permanent housing reconstruction is usually completed within six months of a disaster.
construction_reason: The passage says it often takes 2-3 years.

claim: The flood management guidelines stress preparedness, prevention and mitigation before floods, and prompt response, relief and recovery during and after them.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the stated emphasis.

claim: The new approach gives equal emphasis to preparedness, prevention, mitigation, response and relief, and gives preparedness the largest share of funding.
construction_reason: Equal emphasis is stated; a funding priority is not.

claim: The guidelines keep the earlier relief-centric approach to disaster management.
construction_reason: The passage describes a shift away from the relief-centric approach.

claim: Storm surge is an abnormal rise of water generated by a storm above the predicted astronomical tide, and it causes many of the deaths in tropical cyclones.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the definition and casualty statement.

claim: When a storm surge coincides with high tide, storm tides can reach 6 metres or more, and they occur on average twice a year on the east coast.
construction_reason: The 6-metre storm tides are stated; the twice-a-year frequency is invented.

claim: Floods affect an average of about 40 million hectares in India every year.
construction_reason: The yearly average is about 7.5 million hectares; 40 million is the 1980 estimate of the susceptible area.

claim: Rental accommodation in undamaged existing houses is described as an alternative way of providing temporary shelter, particularly in urban areas.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the rental-accommodation point.

claim: Temporary shelters fall into three typologies, and rental accommodation is the preferred option in both urban and rural areas.
construction_reason: Three typologies are stated; rental is noted for urban contexts, not preferred everywhere.

claim: Assembly-based shelters such as tents and shipping containers are built on site from bricks, stone and cement.
construction_reason: Assembly-based shelters are pre-fabricated elements assembled on site; brick and stone are construction-based.

claim: Because rivers such as the Ganga and Brahmaputra originate in neighbouring countries, information from those countries is needed to manage floods.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the international-information need.

claim: Several expert bodies called for a central organisation to deal with floods, to be run by the Ministry of External Affairs.
construction_reason: The call for a central organisation is stated; MEA control is invented.

claim: Expert committees have advised against a basin approach to flood management.
construction_reason: The committees highlighted the need for a basin approach.

claim: The Brahmaputra Board was set up by the Government of India as a statutory body under the Brahmaputra Board Act, 1980.
construction_reason: Restates the Board's statutory origin.

claim: The MOWR will strengthen the GFCC, completing the work by the end of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan.
construction_reason: Strengthening the GFCC is stated; the completion deadline is not.

claim: The 2004 Task Force recommended winding down the Ganga Flood Control Commission.
construction_reason: The Task Force recommended strengthening it.

claim: Channel improvement has not been widely used in India, mainly because of high costs and topographical constraints.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the stated reasons.

claim: Channel improvement is recommended for entire river lengths to lower flood levels.
construction_reason: It is recommended for local reaches where required, not entire rivers.

claim: Studies confirm a general rise in river beds across India.
construction_reason: The studies do not confirm the belief in a general rise.

claim: A cloudburst is an extreme amount of precipitation in a short period that can create flood conditions.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the definition.

claim: A cloudburst is an extreme amount of rain in a short period, defined as more than 100 mm in one hour.
construction_reason: The definition is supported; the numeric threshold is not in the passage.

claim: A cloudburst is literally the breaking open of a cloud.
construction_reason: The passage says it is not, as sometimes understood, the breaking open of a cloud.

claim: Development that ignores disaster probabilities can worsen existing risks and introduce new ones.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the mainstreaming rationale.

claim: Social inclusion in disaster management means not leaving out community members on the basis of age, gender or disability, with priority given to urban residents.
construction_reason: Inclusion across age, gender and disability is stated; an urban priority is invented.

claim: Mainstreaming DRR means keeping disaster risk reduction separate from development initiatives.
construction_reason: Mainstreaming is the integration of DRR into all developmental initiatives.

claim: A task force set up by the Ministry of Water Resources in August 2004 examined recurring floods in Assam, Bihar, West Bengal and eastern Uttar Pradesh.
construction_reason: Restates the task force's origin and remit.

claim: The 2004 Task Force on flood management was chaired jointly by the Chairman of the CWC and the Chairman of the NDMA.
construction_reason: The CWC Chairman chaired it; an NDMA co-chair is invented.

claim: The listed recommendations called for less emphasis on non-structural measures.
construction_reason: They call for more emphasis on non-structural measures.

claim: Masonry walls in temporary shelters should not rise above sill level (1200 mm), to limit damage in recurring disasters.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the wall-height guidance.

claim: 125 mm thick walls are banned by law in temporary shelters.
construction_reason: Such walls 'should be avoided'; a legal ban is not stated.

claim: Temporary shelter walls should be built well above sill level to give occupants more protection.
construction_reason: Walls should not be taller than sill level.

claim: Diverting part of the floodwater into natural depressions, swamps or lakes can be an economical alternative to dams and reservoirs for flood moderation.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the natural-detention point.

claim: Natural depressions near rivers can moderate floods economically and can replace dams and reservoirs everywhere.
construction_reason: An economical alternative depending on topography is stated; universal replacement is not.

claim: Water stored in reservoirs during floods may not be used for irrigation, power or drinking water.
construction_reason: Stored water is released for irrigation, power generation, drinking and industrial use.

claim: After a flood, a team of a social worker, a psychologist and a psychiatrist is to provide counselling to victims.
construction_reason: Restates the psychosocial provision.

claim: Dead bodies are to be disposed of through district authorities after identification, within six hours of recovery.
construction_reason: Disposal after identification is stated; the six-hour limit is invented.

claim: Documentation of the medical response after a flood is to be done by the district collector.
construction_reason: The passage assigns documentation to a medical administrator.

claim: The WMO defines a heat wave as five or more consecutive days on which the daily maximum temperature exceeds the average maximum by five degrees Celsius.
construction_reason: Restates the WMO definition.

claim: The CWC and the IMD jointly monitor 467 glacial lakes and water bodies in the Indian Himalayan Region.
construction_reason: The CWC monitors 467 lakes; joint IMD monitoring is not stated.

claim: The Lhonak glacier lake shrank from 1.26 km² in 1976 to 0.18 km² by 2013.
construction_reason: The lake grew from 0.18 km² to 1.26 km².

claim: Materials such as stone, bamboo, bricks and wood can be salvaged from debris and reused to build intermediate shelters.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the salvage-and-reuse point.

claim: Salvaged debris materials can be reused for every type of shelter, including permanent housing.
construction_reason: Reuse for intermediate-phase shelters is stated, not for every type including permanent housing.

claim: Bulldozers should clear rubble from damaged house sites before any salvageable materials are collected.
construction_reason: Mechanised clearance should preferably come only after salvageable material is collected.

claim: The IMD and CWC, together with state governments, are to develop forecasting and warning systems for flood-prone areas.
construction_reason: Restates the forecasting responsibility.

claim: The IMD and CWC will develop forecasting and warning systems for flood-prone areas, starting with Rajasthan.
construction_reason: The systems are stated; a Rajasthan-first sequence is not.

claim: Such events have never occurred in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh or Uttar Pradesh.
construction_reason: The passage says such events have also occurred in these states.

claim: At the district level, the DDMA is the nodal agency for coordinating the response, supported by other agencies.
construction_reason: Restates the district-level nodal agency.

claim: The state government activates Incident Response Teams at state, district or block level within one hour of a disaster.
construction_reason: Activation as required is stated; a one-hour deadline is not.

claim: Central ministries direct the response on their own initiative, without waiting for any request from the state.
construction_reason: Central ministries assist as per request from the State/UT.

claim: The plan describes three recovery periods: early (within eighteen months), medium (within five years) and long-term (within five to ten years).
construction_reason: Restates the three recovery periods.

claim: Early recovery is to take place within eighteen months and must restore at least 80 percent of damaged housing.
construction_reason: The eighteen-month period is stated; the 80 percent target is invented.

claim: The NDMP sets fixed recovery timelines for every type of disaster.
construction_reason: The NDMP discusses recovery periods only in general terms without timelines.

claim: Lightweight roofs on temporary shelters should be anchored very well, which is particularly important in cyclone-prone regions.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the roof-anchoring guidance.

claim: Strong joinery lets a house sway as one unit in an earthquake, preventing any damage at all.
construction_reason: Total collapse can be avoided, but the passage says some damage may occur.

claim: Heavy roofs are recommended for temporary shelters in hazard-prone areas.
construction_reason: Preferably no heavy weight roofs should be allowed there.

claim: State governments and SDMAs are to set up websites and portals to share flood-related information with stakeholders.
construction_reason: Restates the dissemination measure.

claim: State governments will make flood information available in multiple formats for different stakeholder groups, including tourists visiting flood-prone areas.
construction_reason: Multiple formats for stakeholder groups are stated; tourists are not mentioned.

claim: Flood risk information is to be kept internal to government agencies rather than shared with stakeholders.
construction_reason: The information is to be disseminated to stakeholder groups.

claim: Section 32 (a) provides that every office at the district level shall prepare a plan setting out prevention and mitigation provisions from the District Plan.
construction_reason: Paraphrases Section 32 (a).

claim: Section 30 (2) (xiv) obliges every District Authority to upgrade its early warning mechanism each year.
construction_reason: The District Authority 'may' set up and upgrade the mechanism; an annual obligation is not stated.

claim: Section 31 (3) (b) excludes prevention and mitigation measures from the District Plan.
construction_reason: It provides that the District Plan shall include such measures.

claim: Road and railway embankments that are not properly aligned and designed can increase an area's vulnerability to flooding and drainage congestion.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the embankment risk.

claim: Sea walls and coastal protection works will be planned and executed by coastal states and port authorities under the supervision of the Indian Navy.
construction_reason: Coastal states and port authorities are named; Navy supervision is invented.

claim: Road and railway embankments reduce drainage congestion wherever they cross drainage lines.
construction_reason: Improperly designed embankments may increase drainage congestion.

claim: The guidelines accept that floods cannot be prevented but say they can be managed to minimise loss of life, livelihoods and property.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the opening premise.

claim: Flood response has been reactive so far, and the guidelines will make it fully preventive by 2010.
construction_reason: The reactive past is stated; a 2010 target is invented.

claim: The guidelines state that floods can be prevented altogether with enough structural works.
construction_reason: The guidelines say floods cannot be prevented.

claim: Under the model bill, the Flood Zoning Authority may direct a land owner or occupier to remove an unauthorised obstruction within a specified time.
construction_reason: Paraphrases Section 24 (1).

claim: The Flood Zoning Authority may direct an owner to remove an unauthorised obstruction, which must be done within seven days.
construction_reason: The time is 'as may be specified'; a fixed seven days is invented.

claim: The model bill gives the Flood Zoning Authority no power to order the removal of obstructions.
construction_reason: Chapter VII grants exactly that power.

claim: The Government of India currently acts as a self-insurer for the National and State Disaster Response Funds.
construction_reason: Restates the self-insurer position.

claim: Relief funds are monitored by the MHA in consultation with the Ministry of Finance and the Reserve Bank of India.
construction_reason: MHA with the Ministry of Finance is stated; the RBI is added.

claim: The Government of India insures the National and State Disaster Response Funds with private insurance companies.
construction_reason: The government acts as a self-insurer.

claim: The NDMP is not an omnibus plan with one budget; it is to be financed from union and state budgets through various ministries and agencies.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the financing approach.

claim: Every ministry, department and state must prepare a DM plan, and every district and village panchayat must also prepare one under the Act.
construction_reason: Ministries, departments and states are named; districts and village panchayats are added.

claim: DRR mainstreaming receives its own separate central budget allocation under the plan.
construction_reason: There cannot be a separate financial allocation for it.

claim: The state governments are to ensure that every flood event is properly documented and its damage assessed on a scientific basis.
construction_reason: Restates the documentation duty.

claim: The highest number of human lives lost to floods in a year was 11,316, in 1977, against an average of 1,587, and the average has since fallen below 500.
construction_reason: The maximum and average are stated; the later fall below 500 is invented.

claim: The largest area affected by floods in a single year was recorded in 1998.
construction_reason: The maximum area affected was in 1978; 1998 is the year of maximum damages.

claim: A compulsory flood-plain insurance scheme would first be tried in a few selected areas on an experimental basis before any wider roll-out.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the experimental introduction of the scheme.

claim: Insurance of structures, buildings and crops in flood plains has been made compulsory.
construction_reason: The MOWR will explore the possibility; the claim states it as an enacted requirement.

claim: Insurance premiums in flood-prone areas are to be the same everywhere, regardless of flood risk.
construction_reason: Studies are to develop premiums graded according to flood risk.

claim: Communities should receive basic training on using shelter kits, including site preparation, foundations and anchors, and repair over time.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the training guidance.

claim: Cash support for hiring labour to assemble shelters is reserved for elderly people.
construction_reason: Cash support for vulnerable people is stated; restricting it to the elderly is not.

claim: Shelter kits should be distributed without any training for the affected communities.
construction_reason: Basic training should be held on using the kits.

claim: In areas liable to flooding in a 25-year flood, residential buildings could be allowed if built on stilts, with minimum plinth levels and no basements.
construction_reason: Restates the 25-year zone stipulations.

claim: In the 25-year flood zone, residential buildings could be permitted on stilts at least 3 metres high.
construction_reason: Construction on stilts is stated; the 3-metre height is invented.

claim: Basements are encouraged for residential buildings in the 25-year flood zone.
construction_reason: Basements are prohibited there.

claim: Capacity development for DRR must go beyond human resource development to address organisational and institutional issues.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the institutional focus.

claim: Partnerships are integral to institutional capacity building, and all capacity development must be delivered through public-private partnerships.
construction_reason: Partnerships are integral; delivering all capacity development through PPPs is not stated.

claim: Capacity development for DRR should focus only on human resource development.
construction_reason: It must go beyond human resource development.

claim: An area is waterlogged when the water table rises enough to saturate the soil pores in the crop root zone, restricting the circulation of air.
construction_reason: Restates the waterlogging definition.

claim: The Irrigation Commission (1972) estimated the area liable to waterlogging at 48.4 lakh hectares, a figure that doubled by 1990.
construction_reason: The 1972 estimate is stated; the later doubling is invented.

claim: Over-irrigation cannot cause waterlogging; only surface flooding can.
construction_reason: Excess rain and/or over-irrigation are named causes.

claim: Although the North Indian Ocean basin generates only about seven per cent of the world's cyclones, their impact is comparatively high.
construction_reason: Paraphrases the share-versus-impact point.

claim: The North Indian Ocean basin generates about seven per cent of the world's cyclones, and the number of cyclones there has doubled since 1990.
construction_reason: The seven per cent share is stated; a doubling since 1990 is not.

claim: A tropical cyclone has winds of at least 100 knots.
construction_reason: The stated threshold is gale force, a minimum of 34 knots.
